summary: Evaluate sandbox-ui design (flat surfaces, weak artifacts, weak brand) vs blueprint-agent workbench + external refs; synthesize a stronger design direction + prioritized build plan

synthesis.designDirection: Direction: "Instrument Deck" — a dark, matte, indigo-tinted instrument backdrop where the substrate is recessive and still, and execution is the only thing that emits light and moves. Three decisions make it coherent and ownable. (1) DEPTH BY LIGHTNESS, NOT HAIRLINES: adopt the already-shipped MD3 violet-tinted surface ladder (#07070d→#0a0a14→#0d0c18→#11101e→#171624→#1f1e30) as the literal z-order — five obviously-distinct planes carrying a Tangle indigo undertone instead of today's three near-identical 5%-saturation grays. Borders demote to edge-light (Geist-style box-shadow rings, not layout borders); floating overlays become the BRIGHTEST surface, fixing today's inversion where dropdowns are darker than the wells they float over. (2) EXECUTION IS THE HIERARCHY: indigo (#6366F1/#818CF8/#A5AAFC) is reserved for structure, intent, navigation and the plan; emerald (#10B981/#34D399) is reserved exclusively for live runtime and freshly-landed output — you read what the machine is doing by where the light is. The signature gesture is the indigo→emerald handoff on an Execution Spine (a 1px circuit-trace thread down the agent timeline, Tangle's knot rendered as a transit line) when a planned step commits to running; the terminal is the one inset, pressed-in well that gains a faint phosphor sheen ONLY while a process runs; Geist Mono is the typographic voice of everything the machine produced or will execute. Nothing glows, pulses, or animates unless real work is happening — every spinner/typing-dot/idle-shimmer is killed for one fill-and-settle motion with an emerald leading edge. (3) THE ARTIFACT IS THE CENTER OF GRAVITY, NOT CHAT: borrow Conductor/Graphite/Primer — a tabbed, diff-first artifact pane (Code · Diff · Preview · Ports · Terminal) with GitHub-Primer diff color science, sticky per-file headers, word-level intra-line highlighting, a change-accounted file tree, and an action row (Copy/Apply/Revert) — so the headline value (an agent that proposes reviewable changes) is finally represented by the panel that currently looks least like it.
synthesis.surfacePlan: Adopt a locked 6-level elevation contract mapped onto the EXISTING `bg-surface*` Tailwind utilities (tailwind.config.cjs:52-63 → @tangle-network/brand --md3-surface*). Zero new CSS, zero node_modules edits, theme-safe (vault light ladder #ffffff→#e1e2e8 inverts correctly). LEVELS: L-1 recessed well `bg-surface-container-lowest` #000001 (terminal viewport, code/log panes); L0 page canvas `bg-surface` #0a0a14 (replaces bg-background #0b0b0d on route shells); L1 structural chrome `bg-surface-container-low` #0d0c18 (top app bar, left nav rail, session sidebar); L2 resting card `bg-surface-container` #11101e (the workhorse — sandbox-card, plan/template cards, resource-meter, dashboard tables, runtime/git/terminal panel containers; replaces ~88 bg-card uses); L3 nested/hover `bg-surface-container-high` #171624 (cards-in-cards, inset toolbars, table-row + nav hover state-layer, status tiles — replaces bg-muted/20–/30 translucent hacks); L4 floating overlay `bg-surface-container-highest` #1f1e30 (popovers, dropdowns, dialogs, command palette, tooltips, notification panel — MUST be lightest, fixing the dashboard-layout.tsx:386 inversion). INPUT WELLS sit one step BELOW their parent: field on a card → `bg-surface-container-low`, field on the page → `bg-surface-dim` #07070d, both with `border-[var(--md3-outline-variant)]` #2a293d lip. BORDERS demote to edge-light: hairlines → `--md3-outline-variant`, emphasized/focus → `--md3-outline` #434260; re-point globals.css .glass-card→var(--md3-surface-container), .glass-panel/.glass-panel-heavy→var(--md3-surface-container), .glass→var(--md3-surface-container-low). Add Geist-style composite elevation: a white-alpha ring (`0 0 0 1px #ffffff14`) + layered negative-spread menu shadow on L4 so small lightness steps register; double focus ring (bg-gap + indigo halo). COMPONENT MAP (sandbox-ui): dashboard-layout.tsx (325 shell→L0; 328 app bar→L1; 386 notification dropdown→L4), app-sidebar.tsx:102,294→L1, session-sidebar.tsx:256→L1 + search input(300)→bg-surface-dim well, sandbox-card/template-card/resource-meter/invoice+sandbox tables/git-panel/runtime-pane→L2 with nested tiles→L3, terminal-panel.tsx:61→L2 + terminal-view.tsx:68 (#0c0c0e)→L-1, all hover:bg-muted→hover:bg-surface-container-high. Selection uses COLOR not lightness: `bg-[var(--accent-surface-strong)]`. Reserve remaining bg-muted for ONE meaning (skeletons/progress tracks/disabled). Add a CI grep guard: overlays never use bg-card, cards never use bg-background. VERIFY on the real app in dark+vault with borders temporarily disabled — depth must survive border:none; confirm on-surface text on #1f1e30 ≥ 4.5:1.
synthesis.artifactPlan: Build one new `SandboxArtifactPane` (new module sandbox-ui/src/workbench/) keeping sandbox-ui's design-system substrate and adding the missing per-artifact VIEW dimension, layering blueprint-agent's orchestration patterns. TWO-TIER TABS: Tier 1 (outer, keep existing FileTabs/ArtifactTabs) = one tab per open artifact with dirty marker + close; Tier 2 (inner, NEW) = an animated PillTabs view switcher Code · Diff · Preview · Ports · Terminal with blueprint's dynamic-visibility + lazy-mount rules. CONTRACT: props { artifact:{id,path,filename,content,baselineContent?,blobUrl?,mimeType?,language?}, gitStatus?, ports?, previewUrl?, terminal?:{apiUrl,token}, activeView?, onViewChange }. VIEWS: CODE = horizontal react-resizable-panels [collapsible RichFileTree (@pierre/trees — git-status decorations/search/context menus; ALREADY installed, exported from src/files) | FilePreview/FileArtifactPane code surface (react-syntax-highlighter — DO NOT add shiki) with a ported FileBreadcrumb header], read-only v1 with a seam for CodeMirror 6 editing later, optional bottom collapsible TerminalView dock. DIFF = @pierre/diffs PatchDiff (sibling of installed @pierre/trees) fed a unified patch from createTwoFilesPatch in the `diff` package; options {diffStyle:'unified', lineDiffType:'word', diffIndicators:'classic', hunkSeparators:'simple', themeType from theme}; header shows filename + green/red +/- counts; Primer dark color science (add bg rgba(46,160,67,0.15)+marker .4, remove bg rgba(248,81,73,0.15)+marker .4, intra-line ~.4, dimmed non-selectable mono gutter); tab hidden unless baselineContent≠content. PREVIEW = iframe bound to previewUrl with a react-query readiness probe (CORS GET poll ~500ms→10s + ~1.5s fallback) + address bar/reload; auto-selected first time a served port appears. PORTS = back with existing src/dashboard/ports-list.tsx (NOT blueprint's previewLinksService), restyled to workbench chrome. TERMINAL = existing src/terminal/terminal-view.tsx, focus-on-activate/fit-on-resize. Non-code kinds collapse Tier 2: markdown→@tangle-network/ui/editor, openui→OpenUIArtifactRenderer. PORT (token-swap bp-elements→shadcn, nanostore→props): pill-tabs.tsx, PanelHeader.tsx, diff.ts (diffFiles), diffUtils.ts (computeDiffStats/getSingleFilePatches) — all from /Users/drew/webb/blueprint-agent/apps/web/src/{components/ui,components/workbench,utils}; reference blocks/diff-viewer/diff-viewer.tsx as the PatchDiff wrapper model. PATTERN-PORT (re-implement, don't copy): Workbench.client view state machine + conditional/lazy-mounted panes, EditorPanel resizable layout, Preview probe, FileBreadcrumb scoped-tree dropdown. DO NOT PORT: blueprint FileTree (RichFileTree is superior), blueprint terminal (have xterm), DiffView worker+react-window+shiki (adds a 2nd highlighter — revisit only for >100KB files). NEW DEPS: `@pierre/diffs`, `diff`. Host the pane via the existing git-panel.tsx / sandbox-workbench.tsx surfaces. ACCEPTANCE: a generated code artifact shows highlighted Code with a git-decorated tree, a word-level unified Diff vs baseline, a readiness-probed Preview, a Ports table, and a working Terminal — switchable via one animated pill bar.
synthesis.brandPlan: Reframe from the brand track: in shipped @tangle-network/brand@0.3.0 the tokens are largely already correct — dark :root sets the --md3-surface* ladder, `--font-display:"Outfit","Geist"` (distinct from `--font-sans:"Geist","DM Sans"`), vault `--font-display:"Manrope","Inter"`, the full status palette (--status-running #10B981, --status-creating #9B93F0, --status-error #FF4D6D), `--md3-surface-tint #818CF8`, dark `--shadow-glow 0 0 32px rgba(99,102,241,0.18)` and `--shadow-status-running 0 0 6px rgba(16,185,129,0.5)`. So brand work is WIRING + ENFORCEMENT, not redefinition. (1) LOAD THE FONTS: ship/import Outfit + Geist Mono (and Manrope for vault) as real webfonts in the consumer — today the families are declared but not loaded, so headings fall back to UI sans; this is why "nothing has voice." (2) ENFORCE THE TYPE LAW: anything machine-emitted or executable (terminal, logs, command names, tool args, file paths, timestamps, token/cost counters, diff gutters) → Geist Mono; product-authored copy → sans; display tier (Outfit) for surface titles/run names/section labels, never marketing-scale inside the workspace. Add a `--font-mono` token if absent. (3) CODIFY THE INDIGO→EMERALD LAW as the one ownable signal: indigo = structure/intent/selection/nav; emerald = live runtime + fresh-output only; never spend emerald on static success chrome or indigo as generic purple. (4) BUILD THE SIGNATURE ELEMENTS in brand/sandbox-ui: an Execution Spine component (1px circuit-trace timeline; pending = dim indigo outline, committed = solid indigo, live = emerald leading-edge, done = settled indigo); terminal-as-lit-well (L-1 surface + phosphor sheen gated on --shadow-status-running ONLY while running; per-line left emerald tick decaying to comment-gray ~2s); one fill-and-settle motion primitive (existing --transition-fast/default/medium 0.1/0.16/0.24s) replacing all spinners/typing-dots; breathing caret only while a stream is open. (5) GATE LIVENESS STRICTLY: --shadow-glow/--shadow-status-running apply only to running entities; idle stays matte; honor prefers-reduced-motion (fills→instant swaps, leading edge→static tick). (6) DO-NOTs: no glass blur / mesh blobs / purple-pink hero gradients (keep --glass-blur 0); no equal-elevation bento cards on flat black; no emoji/traffic-light dots as the only state cue; no Step1/Step2 route narration — the spine + mono output is the narrative. Strengthen the wordmark/logomark (primitives/logo.tsx) with the circuit-trace motif and carry the accent into the product (active session dot, running terminal lines, artifact Apply button).

risks: Brand track was written against a different/older brand snapshot: it claims --font-display collapses to Inter/Geist and --shadow-glow/--shadow-status-running are 'none', but shipped @tangle-network/brand@0.3.0 dark :root already differentiates display and sets both glow tokens. 'Redefine the tokens' work would be wasted; the real gap is fonts-not-loaded + tokens-not-used. Verify the EXACT version the consumer resolves before any token edits.

Theme correctness in vault/light: the surface ladder inverts (#ffffff→#e1e2e8), but indigo→emerald, phosphor sheen, and emerald ticks must be re-tuned for light — emerald/indigo glow on near-white can fail contrast or wash out. Every signature element needs a light pass + 4.5:1 spot-checks.

~88 bg-card + ~130 bg-muted sites are semantically overloaded; a blind find-replace will mis-map (progress-track vs hover vs well). The swap must be intent-aware per the L-1..L4 contract and land with the CI grep guard, or it regresses to a new kind of flat.

Two new deps (@pierre/diffs + diff): @pierre/diffs is beta (sibling @pierre/trees is 1.0.0-beta.3) and may carry breaking changes or theming assumptions that fight the surface tokens; `diff` adds bundle weight. Smoke-test PatchDiff theming against the dark ladder before committing the architecture.

Cross-repo sequencing: brand must publish and the consumer must bump before sandbox-ui/web can use loaded fonts or new tokens. If fonts are added in the web app instead of brand, the design system and the live product drift — decide the ownership boundary up front.

Motion-as-liveness is a strict invariant easy to violate incrementally — one stray idle pulse and 'light means work' collapses. Needs an enforced rule (lint/review checklist) that no animation runs without a backing liveness state, plus prefers-reduced-motion on every fill.

The web consumer path /Users/drew/webb/agent-dev-container/products/sandbox/web/src did not resolve during verification — confirm where the sandbox web app actually imports sandbox-ui and renders the workbench before scoping the integration/proof phase, or the final 'verify on real app' gate has no target.

surfaces.diagnosis: The dark theme reads FLAT because sandbox-ui collapses every surface onto 3 near-identical, desaturated gray tones and then relies on hairline borders to imply depth. Resolved values of the tokens actually in use: bg-background = hsl(240 8% 5%) #0b0b0d (L≈4.7%), bg-card = hsl(240 5% 8%) #141416 (L≈8.2%, used 88x for top-nav, sidebars, cards, terminal panel, AND popovers), bg-muted = hsl(240 5% 11%) #1a1a1d (L≈10.8%, used 130x as an everything-bucket: hover, inset wells, chips, progress tracks, input fills, disabled states). Adjacent layers differ by only ~3.5% lightness at ~5% saturation, which is below the human just-noticeable-difference for large dark fills — so nested cards, sidebars, and panels visually merge and the only separator left is the 7%-opacity border. Two compounding bugs: (1) ELEVATION INVERSION — floating overlays (the notification dropdown in dashboard-layout.tsx:386, most menus) use bg-card (L8.2%) which is DARKER than the inline bg-muted wells they float above (L10.8%), so overlays look like they sit behind the page; (2) bg-muted is semantically overloaded 130x, so it cannot encode a depth level when it simultaneously means hover, fill, track, and disabled. Meanwhile the project already ships a full, violet-tinted MD3 surface-container ladder (--md3-surface* → exposed as bg-surface/bg-surface-container*/etc. utilities in tailwind.config.cjs) with 7 perceptible, progressively tinted steps from L≈0.2% to L≈15.3% — and uses it ZERO times. The fix is not new tokens; it is mapping each component layer onto the existing ladder so depth comes from surface LIGHTNESS (and a subtle indigo elevation-tint), with borders demoted to edge definition rather than the sole depth cue.

proposedElevationLevels.useFor: Terminal viewport, code editor canvas, code blocks, log panes — surfaces that should read as carved BELOW the page plane. var(--md3-surface-container-lowest) = #000001, hsl(240 100% 0.2%). Near-black is ideal for monospace/code contrast. (terminal-view.tsx currently hardcodes #0c0c0e — point it here or keep as a sibling deep value.)

The root page background everything else rests on; full-bleed page shells, empty-state canvases. var(--md3-surface) = #0a0a14, hsl(240 33% 6%). Replaces the current bg-background (#0b0b0d) as the base plane.

proposedElevationLevels.level: L1 — Structural chrome (section / sidebar / app bar)
proposedElevationLevels.useFor: Left nav rail, app/top bar, session sidebar, secondary side panels, page section bands. var(--md3-surface-container-low) = #0d0c18, hsl(245 33% 7%). One clear step above the canvas so the chrome frames the content.

Default content cards and panels: sandbox-card, plan-cards, template-card, resource-meter, dashboard tables, runtime/git/terminal panel containers. var(--md3-surface-container) = #11101e, hsl(244 30% 9%). This is the canonical 'a card' surface — the workhorse that replaces most bg-card usage.

proposedElevationLevels.level: L3 — Nested card / inset toolbar / row hover
proposedElevationLevels.useFor: A card or list-row sitting INSIDE an L2 card, inset toolbars/headers within a panel, table-row hover, the icon tile inside sandbox-card. var(--md3-surface-container-high) = #171624, hsl(244 24% 11%). Gives genuine nested separation (replaces the bg-muted/20–/30 translucent hacks).

Popovers, dropdowns/menus, dialogs/modals, command palette, tooltips, notification panel — anything with a shadow that floats above the app. var(--md3-surface-container-highest) = #1f1e30, hsl(243 23% 15%). MUST be the lightest surface so overlays read ABOVE everything; this fixes the current overlay-uses-bg-card inversion.

proposedElevationLevels.level: Input well (recessed relative to its parent)
proposedElevationLevels.token: bg-surface-container-low (on a card) / bg-surface-dim (on the page)
proposedElevationLevels.useFor: Text inputs, search fields, textareas, select triggers. Sit ONE step BELOW their container for the recessed 'well/track' look: a field on an L2 card uses bg-surface-container-low #0d0c18; a field on the page uses bg-surface-dim #07070d, hsl(240 30% 4%). Pair with border-[var(--md3-outline-variant)] (#2a293d) for a crisp lip. Replaces input/search bg-muted.

proposedElevationLevels.level: Edge / outline (not a fill — replaces border-as-depth)
proposedElevationLevels.useFor: Once layers separate by lightness, borders become edge definition only: outline-variant #2a293d hsl(243 20% 20%) for hairlines between surfaces, outline #434260 hsl(242 19% 32%) for emphasized/focused edges. Demote the current 7%-white --border from primary depth cue to subtle edge.

Step 1 — Lock the 6-level contract in CLAUDE/docs: L-1 lowest (wells/terminal), L0 surface (page), L1 container-low (chrome/sidebars/appbar), L2 container (resting cards), L3 container-high (nested + hover), L4 container-highest (overlays). Every bg-* swap below maps to exactly one level. This is the spec reviewers check against.
Step 2 — Fix the page plane: replace bg-background → bg-surface on route/layout shells (dashboard-layout.tsx:325,455,476; workspace-layout.tsx:252,430). Leaves a 6% canvas for chrome to step off.

surfaces.referenceNotes: How best-in-class dark themes step elevation, and how Tangle's existing tokens already encode it: (1) MD3 dark — the canonical model and the one these tokens implement: each elevation level is a distinct named surface-container that BOTH lightens AND mixes in progressively more surface-tint (the primary hue). Tangle's ladder does exactly this: lowest→highest goes L0.2%→3.9%(dim)→5.9%(surface)→7.1%(low)→9%(container)→11.4%(high)→15.3%(highest), and saturation/indigo-tint rises with height (S 30%→23%, hue parked ~243-245° = the #818CF8 surface-tint). That tint shift is what makes MD3 dark feel 'lit from a soft colored source' rather than flat gray — and it is currently thrown away by using 5%-saturation grays. (2) Linear dark — base ~#08090a, panels step to ~#0e0f11/#16171a in ~3-4% L increments, but Linear ALWAYS pairs the small lightness step with a 1px rgba(255,255,255,~0.08) top-edge highlight + a soft drop shadow, so depth = lightness + edge-light + shadow, never border alone. Lesson for sandbox-ui: small L steps work only with light-edge + shadow; without them you need bigger L steps — which the MD3 ladder provides (5-6% jumps at the card/overlay levels vs the current 3.5%). (3) Vercel/Geist dark — pure neutral scale (#000 background, #0a0a0a cards, then gray-100…gray-400 ≈ #111/#1a1a1a/#222/#333) with deliberately LARGE ~6-8% L steps between interactive layers and crisp hairlines; overlays/menus are clearly the lightest fill. Lesson: when you don't tint, you must make the lightness steps big and unambiguous, and the floating layer must be the brightest. Synthesis for Tangle: adopt the MD3 violet-tinted ladder as-is (it already beats both by combining tint + adequate L steps), enforce overlay = surface-container-highest (brightest, fixing the inversion), and treat the existing --border (7% white) as edge-light, not the depth mechanism. Net: page #0a0a14 → sidebar #0d0c18 → card #11101e → nested #171624 → overlay #1f1e30 gives five obviously-distinct planes vs today's three near-identical grays. artifacts.architecture:
TWO reference systems, one target.

BLUEPRINT-AGENT WORKBENCH (gold standard). State lives in nanostores (workbenchStore: files FileMap, selectedFile, currentDocument, unsavedFiles; themeStore) plus a workbench-layout service that persists the active view and terminal/ports visibility. Shape: a bordered rounded shell with a top toolbar (PillTabs + contextual icon actions + status indicators) over a relative content box holding FOUR absolutely-positioned, framer-motion View panes that slide horizontally (x: 0% active, +/-100% off-screen). Tabs are dynamic: Code is always present; Diff appears only when fileHistory shows real additions/deletions; Preview auto-selects when a dev-server preview is detected; Plugins appears when plugins activate. Diff/Preview/Plugins panes are conditionally MOUNTED (not just hidden) to avoid expensive diff/iframe work on file switches. The Code pane (EditorPanel) is itself a vertical resizable group: [horizontal group: collapsible FileTree | CodeMirror editor with FileBreadcrumb header + Save/Reset] over a collapsible bottom TerminalTabs. So Terminal is NOT a top-level tab there — it is a bottom dock inside Code. Diff is a Web-Worker + react-window + shiki virtualized inline diff. Preview is an iframe with a react-query readiness probe plus a collapsible PortsPane.

SANDBOX-UI (current). The src/{editor,files,openui} barrels re-export a mature design system (@tangle-network/ui ^1.0.1): RichFileTree (Pierre @pierre/trees, git-status decorations, search, context menus, shadow-DOM theming), FilePreview (universal renderer using react-syntax-highlighter for code, plus PDF/CSV/XLSX/markdown/image/text), FileTabs, FileArtifactPane (FileTabs + FilePreview + ArtifactPane chrome + optional Tiptap markdown editor), and OpenUIArtifactRenderer. SandboxWorkbench already wires DirectoryPane + ChatContainer + a per-ARTIFACT tab bar + RuntimePane (which embeds the xterm TerminalView). Crucially there is NO diff dependency anywhere (@pierre/trees is installed, @pierre/diffs is not), no per-artifact Code/Diff/Preview/Ports/Terminal sub-view model, and no live preview iframe. The artifact today is a single FilePreview frame — syntax-highlighted, but flat and view-less — which is why it reads as below the bar.

TARGET. Keep sandbox-ui's design-system substrate (RichFileTree, FileArtifactPane/FilePreview, OpenUIArtifactRenderer, xterm TerminalView, dashboard ports data, ArtifactPane chrome) and add the missing dimension: a per-artifact VIEW tab model (Code/Diff/Preview/Ports/Terminal) layered with the blueprint orchestration patterns (PillTabs, conditional tabs, sliding/mounted panes, resizable tree+editor+terminal). Add a diff capability via @pierre/diffs PatchDiff (consistent with the existing @pierre/trees choice) fed by patches produced with the `diff` package's createTwoFilesPatch — preferring the lighter patch-native path over porting blueprint's worker+react-window+shiki machine, which would import a parallel highlighter (shiki) and conflict with the installed react-syntax-highlighter.
artifacts.diffViewerApproach:
Blueprint ships TWO diff approaches; pick the lighter for sandbox-ui.

(1) Workbench DiffView.tsx = content-pair (before/after strings) -> a singleton Web Worker (diff.worker) computes `unifiedBlocks` with line type (added/removed/unchanged) and char-level charChanges -> react-window FixedSizeList virtualizes the rows at 24px each -> shiki (codeToHtml github-dark/light) highlights only the visible lines, memoized in a process-wide 4096-entry LRU cache, dispatched on a 100ms debounce inside requestIdleCallback. UNIFIED INLINE (single column) with a +/- gutter and per-char highlight on changed lines; fullscreen overlay; binary/error/identical states; +/- counts from diffUtils.computeDiffStats. Heavy but scales to ~1MB files. Strength: huge files + offloaded compute. Cost to adopt: pulls in a worker, react-window, shiki (a SECOND highlighter alongside sandbox-ui's react-syntax-highlighter), and a `diff` dep, all wired to bp-elements tokens and themeStore.

(2) blocks/diff-viewer/diff-viewer.tsx = takes a unified PATCH STRING and renders it through @pierre/diffs PatchDiff with options {diffStyle:'unified', lineDiffType:'word', diffIndicators:'classic', hunkSeparators:'simple', expandUnchanged:false, themeType: light|dark}. Multi-file patches are split with getSingleFilePatches; filename parsed from the +++ header. No worker, no virtualization, no second highlighter. Lighter, patch-native, hunk-aware, word-level intra-line diff.

RECOMMENDATION for sandbox-ui: adopt approach (2). sandbox-ui already depends on @pierre/trees, so @pierre/diffs is the consistent sibling; it needs no worker and no shiki. Feed it patches built from before/after with the `diff` package's createTwoFilesPatch (port diff.ts/diffFiles + diffUtils.getSingleFilePatches verbatim — they are pure functions). Default to a unified inline view to match blueprint; expose a split toggle later if needed. Reserve approach (1) only if multi-hundred-KB generated files become common, in which case wrap PatchDiff/virtualization behind the same Diff-tab contract.
artifacts.tabModel:
Blueprint model: a single PillTabs control over a fixed set of values {code, diff, preview, plugins}, persisted in the workbench-layout store. Tabs are DYNAMIC — Diff is filtered out unless fileHistory has real +/- changes, Plugins unless a plugin is active, and Preview auto-activates when a dev server is detected. Each value maps to one absolutely-positioned framer-motion View that slides on x; Diff/Preview/Plugins are conditionally MOUNTED inside their View so switching files does not pay diff/iframe cost. references.name: Vercel / Geist (vercel.com)

references.name: Graphite (graphite.com)

references.name: GitHub Primer (diff color science baseline)
references.takeaways: The canonical diff grammar Conductor/Graphite refine. Dark add line bg rgba(46,160,67,0.15) + marker rgba(46,160,67,0.4); remove line bg rgba(248,81,73,0.15) + marker rgba(248,81,73,0.4); intra-line token highlight ~0.4 alpha. Low-saturation fills so syntax highlighting stays legible on top. 'Files changed' tree + sticky file headers + per-file viewed checkboxes + rich/source/diff toggles. Line-number gutter dimmed mono, non-selectable.

depthPatterns: Elevation by lightness, not shadow (Linear + Geist): cool near-black canvas at hsl(0,0%,4%) (#0a0a0a, verified Geist bg-100) sitting over pure #000 used ONLY as a recessed well (bg-200). Each elevation step adds ~2-4% L: canvas 4% → card/panel 10% (gray-100) → popover 12% (gray-200) → control-hover 18% (gray-400). Never use flat #000 as the main canvas — a 4-6% base lets borders and elevation register.

Hairline borders as box-shadow rings, not CSS borders (verified Geist): --ds-shadow-border-base dark = '0 0 0 1px #ffffff25' (white at ~14.5% alpha). Implemented as box-shadow so it never affects layout/box size and composes with lift shadows. Recessed wells/inputs use the inset variant 'inset 0 0 0 1px #ffffff1a'. This single technique carries most structure in dark UI.

Layered soft shadows with NEGATIVE spread for floating surfaces (verified Geist --ds-shadow-menu): hairline + '0 1px 1px #00000005, 0 4px 8px -4px #0000000a, 0 16px 24px -8px #0000000f' + a bg-matched outer ring. Three stacked layers of increasing blur; negative spread tightens the penumbra so the shadow hugs the element. Step up to --ds-shadow-2xl ('0 24px 32px -8px #0000000f' tier) for modals. In dark mode raise alpha (Geist medium dark uses #00000052).

The double focus ring (verified Geist --ds-focus-ring = '0 0 0 2px var(--ds-background-100), 0 0 0 4px var(--ds-focus-color)'): a background-colored gap ring first, then the accent ring, so focus reads as a detached halo on ANY surface. Use a brighter accent in dark (blue #50a8ff) than light (#0070f7).

Translucency + backdrop blur for overlay layers (Linear Cmd+K, Conductor macOS vibrancy): overlay/menu background uses an alpha fill over the base PLUS backdrop-filter blur(~20px) saturate(~180%) so the layer beneath bleeds through — perceived depth and native feel without a hard opaque card. Geist ships backdrop-blur tokens for this.

Composite elevation tokens — bundle hairline + lift + bg-ring into ONE box-shadow value (Geist --ds-shadow-border-medium = border-base + shadow-medium + background-border) and reuse the same token across every floating element. Guarantees consistent depth language and avoids ad-hoc shadow drift.

Small-radius discipline (verified Geist --geist-radius: 6px base): tight radii with nested radii decreasing inward read as 'engineered dev-tool', not 'marketing card'. Reserve large radii for hero/marketing only.

Material differentiation for code: the code/diff surface should be a visibly distinct, MORE recessed material than the surrounding chrome (e.g. pure #000 / bg-200 well behind monospace), reinforcing that artifacts are 'inset' into the workbench rather than floating on it.
artifactPatterns: File tree with change accounting (Conductor/Graphite/Primer): left rail lists changed files; each row = dimmed directory path + bright filename, a +N/−M pair in green/red monospace, and a status glyph (A/M/D/R). Collapsible by directory; selected row gets a translucent accent fill + a left accent bar. Virtualize for large diffs.

Sticky per-file headers in the diff scroll (Conductor/Graphite/Primer): as you scroll a multi-file diff, each file's path header pins to the top of the viewport. Header carries a collapse chevron, path as a breadcrumb (chevron separators, last segment bold), +/− counts, a 'viewed' checkbox, and an overflow menu.

Split vs unified toggle (Graphite/Conductor): segmented control in the diff toolbar; split = two gutters + two aligned code columns, unified = single column with +/− prefixes. Persist the choice. Add word-level intra-line highlighting — brighter green/red on the exact changed tokens within a changed line.

Diff line color science (Primer dark, used by Conductor): add line bg rgba(46,160,67,0.15) with marker/gutter rgba(46,160,67,0.4); remove line bg rgba(248,81,73,0.15) with marker rgba(248,81,73,0.4); intra-line token highlight ~0.4 alpha. Keep fills low-saturation so syntax colors stay legible. Line-number gutter in dimmed mono, non-selectable.

Tabs/cards for parallel artifacts or agent workspaces (Conductor): top strip of tabs, each with name + status dot (running = pulsing accent, needs-review = amber, done = green check) + dirty indicator. Active tab uses translucent fill + a bottom accent underline. Center = activity/conversation, right or overlay = the diff/artifact.

Code surface as a first-class material: monospace (Geist Mono / SF Mono), a more-recessed background than chrome, generous line-height (~1.5), a dark-tuned syntax theme (desaturated pastels, not neon). On hover expose copy + wrap-toggle; keep the filename sticky.

Breadcrumb + command navigation for large diffs (Graphite): repo › branch › file breadcrumb at top; j/k or ↑/↓ jump file-to-file; a 'next unviewed' key; a progress affordance ('3 of 12 files · 2 viewed') or minimap. Keyboard-first review.

Inline comment/annotation threads anchored to lines (Graphite/Conductor review): hovering a line reveals a + in the gutter; threads render as inset cards indented under the line with a connecting hairline; resolved threads collapse to a chip. Threads live INSIDE the diff flow, not in a separate panel.

Artifact pane that can pop full-width or dock-split (Linear side panel + Claude artifacts): slides in from the right as an overlay over a dimmed+blurred main, OR docks as a resizable split. The drag handle is a 1px hairline that thickens to the accent color on hover. The pane is first-class, resizable, and keyboard-dismissible.
distinctiveElements: Conductor: real macOS vibrancy sidebar (NSVisualEffectView material that picks up wallpaper tint, not faux dark CSS), unified titlebar with traffic lights, parallel-agents-as-isolated-workspaces (each own branch/terminal/diff) surfaced as tabs, and a warm Claude coral accent (~#d97757) deliberately set against cool neutral surfaces. The diff/review/merge flow — not chat — is the visual center of gravity.

Linear: Cmd+K command menu as frosted-glass overlay, ubiquitous KBD shortcut chips, a contextual right-side panel sliding over a dimmed canvas, the muted gray-blue text ramp (#f7f8f8 / #8a8f98), the sparingly-used #5e6ad2 brand purple, depth carried by hairlines + lightness with almost no in-app drop shadows, and buttery subtle scale+fade panel transitions. Aurora gradient glows confined to marketing heroes only.

Vercel/Geist: the triadic dark scale (#0a0a0a canvas / #000 well / white-alpha hairlines), the signature double focus ring (bg gap + blue halo), shadow tokens authored as border+lift+bg-ring composites, the Geist + Geist Mono pairing with monospaced numerics in dashboards, deploy/workflow steps rendered as labeled timing chips (420ms/252ms), a tight 6px base radius, and a p3/oklch color upgrade path.

Graphite: the vertical 'stack rail' — connected nodes drawing a PR stack as a spine down the left edge — plus a stack-aware merge queue, fully keyboard-driven file-to-file review (j/k, next-unviewed), persistent per-file 'viewed' state, word-level intra-line diff highlighting, inline threads as inset cards, and a neon-hex glow brand motif on dark.

GitHub Primer: the de-facto diff grammar everyone refines — add/remove line bg + marker alpha science, the 'Files changed' tree with sticky file headers and per-file viewed checkboxes, rich/source/diff view toggles, and a dimmed non-selectable mono line-number gutter. The baseline the others build on top of.

currentWeaknesses: The tokens explicitly zero out every depth and liveness cue: --glass-blur:0px, --shadow-glow:none, --shadow-status-running/creating/error:none, --mesh-teal/violet/blue:transparent, and a uniform --shadow-card:0 1px 2px. The product is flat by configuration, not by accident — elevation carries no meaning and nothing on screen signals that work is happening.

Two divorced depth systems coexist. A rich indigo-tinted MD3 surface stack (#07070d -> #0a0a14 -> #11101e -> #171624 -> #1f1e30) ships unused alongside a desaturated neutral working stack (--bg-root:#0b0b0d, --depth-1..4: #0b0b0d..#202023). The chrome is almost certainly painted from the neutral grays, so it reads as default-dark-SaaS instead of Tangle dark.

--font-display collapses to "Inter","Geist" — identical to --font-sans — despite the README specifying Outfit (dark) and Manrope (vault) as the display families. There is no typographic hierarchy: headings, run names, and body all render in the same UI sans, so nothing has voice or rank.

A complete execution-state palette is defined but expressed as nothing more than dots: --status-running #10B981, --status-creating #9B93F0, --status-warm #FF8A4C, --status-cold #4AABFF, --status-stopped #FFB800, --status-error #FF4D6D, plus a full syntax palette. Color is not doing semantic work; state is invisible at a glance.

Indigo and emerald are present but used decoratively and interchangeably. There is no law separating the agent's intent/structure from live runtime, so the one color relationship that could own the 'visible execution' moat is wasted as generic brand-purple-plus-success-green.

Motion is undefined for streaming. Without a signature, the product will default to generic spinners, three-dot typing indicators, and skeleton shimmer — the exact vocabulary that makes an execution product look like a chat skin and hides the runtime that is the moat.
brand.proposedDirection: Direction: \"Instrument Deck\" — the UI is a dark, matte, indigo-tinted instrument backdrop on which execution is the only thing that emits light. Commit to one law: the substrate (rails, panels, chrome, idle state) is recessive, near-black, and still; state and motion (running terminals, the advancing agent timeline, streaming tokens, materializing artifacts) are the bright, saturated, moving foreground. Nothing glows, pulses, or moves unless it is actually doing something. This turns \"visible execution\" from a feature panel into the literal visual hierarchy of the whole product — you read what the machine is doing by where the light is. Repaint the chrome from the unused indigo-tinted MD3 surface stack (not the neutral grays) so the dark reads unmistakably as Tangle, and codify a strict two-hue grammar: indigo is structure and intent (the plan, the potential, what the agent means to do); emerald is kinetic runtime (the plan actually executing, real output landing). The signature moment of the entire product is the indigo->emerald handoff when a planned step commits to execution. One coherent direction, ruthlessly applied — instrument, don't decorate.
signatureElements: The Execution Spine: a single continuous 1px thread down the left edge of the agent timeline (Tangle's knot rendered as a circuit trace / transit line). Tool calls, command runs, and file writes are nodes on it. Pending segments are dim indigo outline; committed-to-run segments fill solid indigo; the live segment pulses emerald with a leading edge; completed work settles to solid indigo. The whole run is legible as one advancing thread, not a scrollback of chat bubbles.

Terminal-as-lit-instrument: the runtime/terminal pane is the one surface treated as an inset, pressed-in well (everything else is on-top), carrying a faint top-down phosphor sheen ONLY while a process runs. Each freshly emitted output line gets a left-edge emerald tick that decays to comment-gray over ~2s, so the eye catches exactly what just happened. Idle terminal is matte and dark with no sheen — 'is it running?' becomes a glance-level read.

The indigo->emerald state law as an ownable signal: indigo family (#6366F1 / #818CF8 / #A5AAFC) is reserved for structure, selection, navigation, and the agent's intent; emerald (#10B981 / #34D399) is reserved for live execution and real output landing. Hue alone tells you intent vs. action; the transition between them on the spine is the brand's signature gesture.

Mono as the voice of the runtime: a strict type law where anything the machine produced or will execute (terminal, logs, command names, tool args, file paths, timestamps, token/cost counters) is Geist Mono, and anything the product says about it is sans. The execution moat becomes visible typographically, before any color or motion loads.

The advancing-fill motion signature replacing all spinners: streaming tokens, spine fill, terminal output, and progress all share one left-to-right / top-to-bottom fill-and-settle with a brief emerald leading edge that settles to the resting color — so the entire product feels like one physical process advancing, never N independent spinners.
brand.typeColorMotion: TYPE: Activate the display tier that already exists but collapses. Outfit for display/orientation (surface titles, run names, section labels) with tight tracking; Geist for UI body; Manrope for display in the vault light theme. Geist Mono is the runtime voice — every machine-emitted or executable string is mono, every product-authored string is sans. Display is for orientation, not marketing-scale heroes inside the workspace. COLOR: Repaint backgrounds from the indigo-tinted MD3 stack — root #07070d, canvas #0a0a14, panel #11101e, elevated #171624 — so the dark carries a Tangle undertone instead of neutral black. Indigo = structure/intent (#6366F1 primary action, #818CF8 interactive/selection, #A5AAFC emphasis/links). Emerald = live execution only (#10B981 running, #34D399 fresh-output tick); never spend it on static success chrome. The status palette is the complete execution vocabulary and the ONLY family permitted to pulse: creating #9B93F0, running #10B981, warm #FF8A4C, cold #4AABFF, stopped #FFB800, error #FF4D6D. Coral #FF4D6D is reserved exclusively for execution failure. MOTION: One easing, one behavior — fill-and-settle with an emerald leading edge, cadence matched to data arrival, never slower than the stream. Re-enable a restrained glow but gate it strictly on liveness (override --shadow-status-running from none to a tight emerald ring; idle entities stay matte). Indeterminate waiting = a slow indigo shimmer traveling a border (the carrier signal); determinate progress = emerald fill. Kill spinners and typing dots; the breathing caret appears only while a stream is open. Honor prefers-reduced-motion: fills become instant state swaps, the leading edge becomes a static tick, the caret becomes solid. Use existing --transition-fast/default/medium (0.1/0.16/0.24s) for UI transitions.
doNots: Do not paint chrome from the neutral --depth/--bg grays (#0b0b0d..#202023); that is the source of the generic-dark read. Use the indigo-tinted MD3 surface stack instead.
Do not reintroduce glassmorphism blur, mesh-gradient blobs, or purple-to-pink hero gradients. The tokens correctly zeroed --glass-blur and --mesh-*; leave them dead.
Do not float equal-elevation cards on flat near-black, and do not build a bento grid of stat cards. Elevation must mean liveness, not z-order or layout convenience.
Do not use generic spinners, three-bouncing-dot typing indicators, or ambient skeleton shimmer as the streaming language — that is the chat-skin tell that buries the runtime.
Do not spend emerald as decorative success green or indigo as generic brand purple everywhere; that collapses the intent-vs-execution signal that is the whole point.
Do not add any motion that runs while nothing is executing — no idle pulses, no ambient gradient drift, no breathing logos. Motion must always mean work is happening.
Do not render the terminal or logs as just another raised card, and do not bury runtime output in a collapsed drawer treated as debug. The runtime is the moat surface, not secondary output.
Do not narrate execution with label-heavy 'Step 1 / Step 2 / Route' chrome; the spine plus mono output is the narrative. No emoji status icons; no traffic-light dots as the only state cue.
Do not let display type collapse back into the body sans, and do not use marketing-scale headings inside the product workspace. Headings orient; they do not decorate.

findings.issue: The artifact pane is subtitled "Suggested fix — retry logic" (sb-workspace-full.png) yet renders as a plain, un-annotated code block. There are zero diff signals: no +/- gutter, no green/red add/remove lines, no changed-line highlight, no before/after. The product's headline value (an agent that proposes code changes — conductor-quality artifacts) is represented by the one panel that least looks like it. It reads as a static snippet, not a reviewable change.
findings.fix: Render this as a real unified diff: add a left gutter with line numbers + change markers, tint added lines with a green wash (e.g. rgba(63,185,80,0.12)) and a 2px left accent, removed lines red wash. Since the whole function is "the fix," show 2–3 lines of unchanged context then the changed block highlighted, so the eye lands on what changed. This single change resolves the owner's "weak artifact" concern more than any styling.

findings.issue: The sessions rail, chat column, terminal, and artifact pane all sit on the same near-black value, divided only by uniform 1px hairlines. There is no surface ramp, no shadow, and no top-edge inner highlight — so the UI reads as one flat sheet with lines drawn on it rather than stacked planes. The owner's "flat, same dark bg on every component, no elevation" is accurate and visible across all three shots.
findings.fix: Introduce a 3-step surface ramp: app bg darkest (~#0A0B0F), panel surfaces one step up (~#111319), cards/bubbles/terminal one step higher (~#16181F). Add a 1px top inner-highlight (border-top: rgba(255,255,255,0.06)) on panels and cards for the glassy lit-edge, and a soft ambient shadow on raised cards (0 1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.4), 0 8px 24px -12px rgba(0,0,0,0.6)). Keep hairline borders but let value + light do the depth work.

findings.issue: The hero (new-hero-tall.png) is a generic dark dev-tool template: white bold headline, indigo primary button, outline secondary, subtle blue radial bg. Nothing is ownable — no signature accent, no motif, no glow, no distinctive type. Against the Modal reference (vivid emerald + 3D extruded-cube motif + neon-glow panels) and E2B (terminal-forward identity), this has no visual fingerprint. Swap the wordmark and it's indistinguishable from a dozen YC infra landing pages.
findings.fix: Commit to one signature system: pick a distinctive accent pairing (not stock indigo) and a repeatable motif tied to "a real machine" — e.g. an isometric/extruded sandbox-container or port-grid mark, a signature glow color applied to the primary CTA and the active session/running state, and a brand gradient used consistently on the headline accent and CTA. Carry that accent into the product (active session dot, running terminal lines, artifact apply button) so the embedded workspace reinforces the brand instead of being neutral gray.

findings.issue: The code in the artifact pane is rendered near-monochrome (light gray on dark). Keywords (async, function, const, for, try, catch, return, throw), numbers (5, 200, 10_000), and types (RetryOptions, Record) are essentially uncolored. A code workspace whose entire pitch is code looks like a text file. This compounds the "weak artifact" concern.
findings.fix: Apply a real syntax theme (keyword/control, string, number, type, function-call, comment all distinctly colored) tuned to the dark surface. Even a restrained 5–6 color theme dramatically raises the credibility of the panel and is cheap to add.

findings.issue: In new-hero-workspace2.png the code is hard-clipped at the right edge with no affordance: "attempt < att…" and "...baseDelayMs * 2 ** (attempt - 1) + jitter," are cut mid-token with nothing indicating scrollability. It reads as a broken/overflowing layout, not an intentional horizontal scroll.
findings.fix: Either soft-wrap long lines with a hanging indent, or add an explicit horizontal scroll affordance (fade mask on the right edge + thin scrollbar). Given the embed width, soft-wrap is the safer default so no token is silently truncated in the marketing shot.

findings.issue: In new-hero-workspace2.png the strict-equality operator renders as a solid bar/strikethrough glyph: "if (attempt ▬▬▬ maxAttempts)". A code-font ligature (or a font lacking the glyph) is collapsing === into a block, which looks like a rendering bug in a panel that's supposed to showcase code quality.
findings.fix: Disable programming-ligatures on the code surface (font-variant-ligatures: none; font-feature-settings: "liga" 0, "calt" 0) or switch to a mono font that renders === cleanly. Verify the screenshot afterward — this is a literal visible defect.

findings.area: Hero — figure/ground separation of the mockup
findings.issue: In new-hero-tall.png the workspace mockup sits in a flat dark rounded frame on an equally dark page background, with minimal contrast between the two. The product — the thing you most want to sell — nearly camouflages into the page and doesn't pop. The Modal reference separates its panels with glow and lighter card surfaces; here there's none.
findings.fix: Lift the mockup off the page: lighter frame surface than the page bg, a subtle outer glow/colored shadow in the brand accent, and/or a faint gradient halo behind it. Add a thin lit top border on the frame. The mockup should clearly be the brightest, most-elevated object in the hero.

findings.issue: In sb-workspace-full.png the chat column has a large empty void between the last assistant message (~y=325) and the input box (~y=635), and the artifact column is mostly empty below the code. Content is top-aligned into a tall viewport, so the panels look unfinished/under-filled rather than dense and alive.
findings.fix: Right-size the embed height to the content, or fill the space meaningfully: pin the composer to the bottom of the chat pane (so the gap is intentional whitespace, not a void), and let the terminal grow to occupy the remainder. For the artifact column, add the diff chrome (tabs, footer toolbar) so it reads as a full panel, not a short snippet floating in black.

findings.issue: Beyond the diff itself, the artifact panel lacks every affordance of a real artifact/conductor viewer: no tabs (Diff / Code / Preview), no line numbers, no language/file-type badge, no file-path breadcrumb, and no action row (Copy, Apply, Revert, Open in editor). It's an eyebrow + title + raw code — far below "conductor-quality."
findings.fix: Add a panel header row with a tab strip (Diff active) and a right-aligned action cluster (Copy, Apply fix), line numbers in the gutter, and a small language badge (TS). This is what makes it read as an interactive artifact surface rather than a code dump, and directly answers the owner's reference to a tabbed/diff viewer.

findings.issue: In new-hero-workspace2.png a purple user bubble is half-clipped between the assistant message and the composer, peeking out as a sliver. It reads as an overflow/z-index accident, adding noise directly above the input where the eye rests.
findings.fix: Mask the scroll region cleanly (overflow hidden with a bottom fade) so partial messages fade out instead of being hard-cut, or adjust the seeded conversation/height so a bubble doesn't land half-visible in the marketing crop.

findings.issue: The storybook full view (sb-workspace-full.png) shows an agent identity header "Blueprint Agent / tangle.network" at the top of the rail, but the hero embed (new-hero-workspace2.png) shows only a lone chat-bubble icon with large empty padding and no agent name. The same component renders two different, weaker states; the hero crop loses the identity anchor and the floating icon reads as ambiguous.
findings.fix: Keep the agent identity block (avatar + name + org) visible in the hero embed too, or replace the lone icon with the proper header. Ensure the marketing crop shows the populated state, not a degraded one.

findings.issue: The terminal pane uses the exact same background value as the chat column above it; only the "TERMINAL" label and a hairline separate them. Terminals conventionally get a distinct, slightly different surface, which would also reinforce the elevation system.
findings.fix: Give the terminal a distinct treatment: a marginally darker/cooler surface, a header toolbar (label + actions), and optionally a faint top inner-highlight. Pairs with the elevation-ramp fix and makes the panel read as its own plane.

findings.issue: The hero subcopy is a flat feature enumeration: "Provision an isolated Linux workspace with agents, shell, files, ports, desktop, and trace capture. Launch from the dashboard, SDK, or CLI." It lists capabilities instead of landing a sharp value proposition, and the comma-list dilutes the strong headline.
findings.fix: Lead with the outcome/why, then let features be secondary (e.g. a one-line benefit + a compact capability row or icon list below). Avoid the six-item inline comma list directly under the headline.

findings.issue: The green/gray/red status dots and the "PINNED" pill are tiny and low-emphasis. The running/idle/failed signal is one of the few pieces of product personality on screen (live, multi-session machine) yet it's barely legible at hero scale.
findings.fix: Strengthen the status system: slightly larger dots, a subtle pulse/glow on the active (green) session tied to the brand accent, and a clearer failed (red) treatment. This both improves scannability and becomes a brand-reinforcing live detail.

findings.issue: The "Tangle Sandbox" wordmark in the top nav (new-hero-tall.png) is small undifferentiated text with a faint mark; it provides a weak brand anchor and competes poorly with the nav links beside it.
findings.fix: Give the wordmark a distinctive treatment tied to the brand motif/accent chosen in the brand fix — a stronger logomark and clearer lockup so the brand registers at first glance.
